text: Lesson One — Coastal Walk Twas checking the route of a coastal walk I was going to do. I noticed that one area was a*favourite spot for fishing’ - awesome, I love sea fishing and get inordinately excited when I find a new potential fishing spot. Anyway, a few days later I was on the beach walking the actual route, taking in the sca air and how free I was, when I noticed ahead of me around twenty people fishing from a hundred-metre section of beach; the previous five miles from where I'd started the walk, I hadn’t seen any of the smelly fuckers. T realised this was the *favourite fishing spot” stretch of beach that I had found out about a couple days carlier You may not know that it is impossible for a fisherman to walk past another one without asking variations of these four questions; 1 What are you fishing for? 2 Much luck? 3 What bait are you using? 4 Do you own bitcoin? (Ok, I made-up that last one but I might start using it for a laugh). T stopped to talk to a guy and his wife who were fishing. I told them I had seen online that this was a good fishing spot (confirmed by the amount of people fishing), why was that? “Is there a wreck out there?” Fish congregate around wreck. “Or a hollow where fish colleet?”. “No”, the bloke replied, “we fish here because there’s a toilet over there, and a place which sells tea and coffec”. This made me laugh my fucking head off. I'd assumed the reason people fished there was something to do with fish, how wrong was 1 it was nothing to do with fish. The “favourite fishing spot’ was because of the refreshments and being able to go for a crap. If you're an entrepreneur, business owner or anyone who makes money from clients customers, a market, whatever...don't make the mistake I made. My knowledge of fishing had made me assume there was a fish related answer to a particular situation which involved fishing, I hadn't realised there may be non-fish reasons for it. Worse: it's possible that my knowledge of fishing made me less open to other scenarios Life has a million connections, many of which are under the radar. Don't let your knowledge of a subject make you blind This was a fabulous lesson, one which I'll never forget.
